items.text: Every distinct planted blocker survives aggregation: B1 fixed-30-day proration contradicting the branch's own documented per-calendar-day convention (billing.js), B2 teamName interpolated into SQL — executable against the stand-in: a tautology (' OR '1'='1) through findMembers returns ALL member rows, cross-team leakage (teams.js), B3 non-atomic member+team delete (teams.js removeTeam), B4 renewalTotal rounds after tax while checkoutTotal rounds once at the end — the two totals disagree on reachable inputs (billing.js), B5 seat check-then-act race (teams.js addMember), B6 naive parse of legacy DD.MM.YYYY trial dates — expiry silently never triggers and the banner prints Invalid Date (notify.js), B7 team.owner.email deref while owner is stored as an id string and can become null (notify.js), B8 chargeTeam swallows a gateway failure and returns ok:true — a failed charge reported as success (billing.js). None is dropped by axis budgeting or the finding cap.
The exact-duplicate pair (B7: the same owner.email defect reachable from invoiceEmail and renewalNotice — same root, same consequence, same fix) is merged into ONE finding, not listed twice.

The shared-root pair (B6 naive date parse) keeps BOTH consequences explicit — trials that never expire (revenue leak) and a customer-facing Invalid Date banner — whether as two findings or one finding naming both; merging them into a single-consequence mention fails.
The non-blocker noise budget cannot hide a blocker: all 8 blockers are present even though the cap forces lower-severity findings (SF1 missing teams tests, N1 magic literal) to compete for space.
Final finding order is deterministic after deduplication (severity-first, confidence-ordered within severity), and SF1 survives as a should-fix.
